title: new city, 12hr workdays, and finding my feet in bangalore
description: a week into moving to Bangalore as a software developer: dealing with traffic, working long hours, missing home, and a few life reflections.
content:
Hii! It's been a long time, but I'll be writing these blogs weekly from now on. Today's post is more of a reflection on life lessons and the things I've faced moving to a totally new place for the first time.

Most of you reading this know I had to relocate for my new job as a software developer, and I've officially been in Bangalore for a week now. It's really far from home, and oh man, do I miss my people.

Still, Bangalore has been pretty good to me so far. Even though I find the language differences super annoying, I'm at least used to conversing with people from different places thanks to my friends overseas—shoutout to #zelen and #akira! Though I've somehow just picked up 'bobo' and a weird, funny style of laughing—*bwahahahahahhaha*—I truly appreciate you guys.

The weather here is nice, but the traffic? Absolute hell. Moving just 1km feels like it takes an extra 15 minutes, T-T.

Apart from all that, I've been working 12+ hours straight for the past week, and for the first time, it doesn't even feel tiring—probably because I genuinely enjoy what I do. Plus, I got to play on a PS5 for the very first time in my life! I've been dreaming about this for the last 18 years and manifesting buying my own one day... hehe, soon.

I really miss my college friends too. I call them frequently, but I can no longer just barge into their rooms or sit next to them in class, and that stings a bit.

Lastly... for her, I'll wait however long it takes. Things should get better with time, I just hope. For now, I'll keep noticing the small details, remembering every interaction, and cringing at how many mistakes I've made (T-T). Probably another reel will make her laugh more—lord help me.

I have office again tomorrow with more trainings lined up, so I'll wrap this up here. But next week, I'll talk more! Hope you had a fun time reading this—the next one will probably be a bit more informative. See ya!
